skins.style_brief: Eurylochus, Odysseus's blunt second-in-command (Odyssey Book 9). A weathered, sun-cured ship's officer: full grey-streaked dark beard, a rust-red exomis tunic cinched by a worn leather belt, bare tanned arms and legs, plain deck sandals. Reads as older, authoritative, out of patience.

Perimedes, the quiet strong hand of Odysseus's crew (Odyssey Book 9). A younger deckhand with a short near-black beard and hollow, sleepless eyes; a sea-teal exomis over sea-paled skin, a dark rope-and-leather belt, worn sandals. Reads as steady but haunted.

Antiphos, the grim old veteran of Odysseus's crew (Odyssey Book 9). The oldest hand left at the campfire: a heavy iron-grey beard gone nearly white, a deeply sun-cured and scarred face, a faded ochre-brown exomis worn thin over hard lean muscle, a scuffed wide leather belt, old cracked sandals. Reads as weathered, watchful, and out of illusions.

Elpenor, the unlucky youngest of Odysseus's crew (Odyssey Book 9). A green farm-boy turned oarsman: clean-shaven or barely stubbled, an open frightened young face, pale-under-tan skin freckled by the sun, a cheap undyed cream exomis gone grey with salt, a thin cord belt, plain sandals. Reads as too young for this and knowing it.
